mechanism_narrative: Accelerating decline in WORKPLACES mobility over four consecutive weeks signals sustained workplace closures or remote-work adoption. This reduces commuter foot traffic and associated retail incidence, driving RETAIL_REC further negative over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES declined from -5.3% to -19.9% over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases or remains flat over the next 28 days despite WORKPLACES continuing to decline week-on-week.

mechanism_narrative: Rising RESIDENTIAL mobility coupled with declining RETAIL_REC indicates consumers are consolidating trips and substituting in-store shopping with delivery or online channels. This substitution effect persists, keeping RETAIL_REC depressed over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL rose from 7.0% to 13.7% while RETAIL_REC fell from -16.1% to -29.1%
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC reverses to positive territory over the next 28 days while RESIDENTIAL remains elevated above 12%.

mechanism_narrative: Mid-December holiday shopping demand typically peaks in retail, but TRANSIT mobility collapse (from -15.1% to -27.0%) indicates transport constraints preventing access to retail venues. candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls below -25% for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT declined from -15.1% to -27.0% over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above -15% in the next two weeks despite TRANSIT remaining below -25%.

candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM exceeds RETAIL_REC by more than 40 percentage points
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC and GROCERY_PHARM converge to within 20 percentage points over the next 28 days, indicating policy relaxation.

evidence_refs: fact:PARKS at -23.7% in most recent week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rebounds above -20% in the next week while PARKS remains below -22%.

evidence_refs: fact:All three series declined sharply in t-0w
